name: CBD
short: Cannabidiol, a major non-intoxicating cannabinoid sold in hemp products and approved in purified form as the prescription drug Epidiolex.
definition: CBD, or cannabidiol, is the second best-known cannabinoid after THC. It does not cause a high, which is why it became the backbone of the hemp consumer market after the 2018 Farm Bill: oils, creams, capsules, drinks and pet products. A purified CBD medicine, Epidiolex, is the only FDA-approved drug derived from the cannabis plant and is prescribed for certain rare seizure disorders.

The retail picture is messier. The FDA has concluded that CBD cannot be marketed as a dietary supplement and that adding it to food sold across state lines is prohibited, although enforcement has focused mainly on companies making disease claims. Federal health researchers note that over-the-counter products may contain more or less CBD than labelled and sometimes contain THC, and that CBD can cause side effects and interact with other medicines.

In the European Union, CBD foods are treated as novel foods that need authorisation before sale. In February 2026 the European Food Safety Authority set a cautious provisional safe level for highly purified CBD supplements while repeating that important safety data gaps remain. In the US, hemp CBD products also face the new 0.4 mg total-THC per-container cap from 11 December 2026, which matters for full-spectrum products containing traces of THC.
example: The ruling means CBD snacks must clear EU novel-food approval before they can carry an organic label.
